name: room
text: Room opened — goal: memory: Recall by meaning, relate elements, build the brain graph, embed unembedded elements.

name: Graft
text: To achieve our goal of recalling by meaning and building the brain graph, I think we should start by identifying and grouping related concepts. This approach allows us to create a foundation for meaningful connections and relationships between elements, making it easier to embed unembedded elements later on. By focusing on concept grouping first, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially delayed progress on embedding individual elements, but this foundation will ultimately lead to a more solid and interconnected brain graph. This decision prioritizes the quality of our brain graph's structure over rapid embedding of individual elements.

name: Prune
text: Prune: I hear the value in grouping concepts upfront, but the real risk is forcing premature structure—what if the relationships we assume today blind us to the ones that emerge later? A better alternative might be to first surface raw, unfiltered associations (like free-form brain dumps) before imposing any hierarchy. That way, we avoid anchoring on early groupings and only formalize what proves durable. Settle it by testing both: try the free-form approach for a set of concepts, then see if the groupings we’d have imposed initially still hold weight after the fact.
